August 27, 2024 Reducing Risk for Dementia Purpose There are common conditions and lifestyle behaviors that can increase your risk for dementia. Learn what they are and the healthy lifestyle habits that can lower your risk of developing dementia, including Alzheimer's disease. Risk factors There are known factors that can increase your risk of dementia. These include: Lack of physical activity. Uncontrolled diabetes. High blood pressure. Hearing loss. Tobacco and alcohol use. Racial/ethnic differences A recent study found that certain racial/ethnic groups, including African American, Hispanic, and American Indian and Alaska Native adults, were more likely to have these risk factors. 1 This is important, because those same racial/ethnic groups are also more likely to develop dementia than other groups. After bushwhacking hundreds of miles in sandals, he was used to such insults to his 52-year-old feet. But this was the mother of all splinters. It bounced off a bone, lodged in a tendon, and refused to come out. Finally his hiking partner, Lindsey Holm, grabbed it with a pair of pliers and after several sharp tugs, yanked it free. "You could hear me yelling from mountaintop to mountaintop," Fay says. "It was one of the most painful things I've ever experienced." Which is something coming from a man who was once gored 16 times by an elephant. He taped up the wound, shouldered his pack, and as he had for the past three months, kept walking. pages.description: Former West Ham and Augsburg defender Reece Oxford signs for League One strugglers Bromley.
pages.text: Reece Oxford: Bromley sign ex-West Ham defender - BBC Sport Image source, Shutterstock Image caption, Reece Oxford last played a competitive professional game of football four years ago By Ben Ashton BBC Sport England Published 2 hours ago League One strugglers Bromley have signed former West Ham defender Reece Oxford on a free transfer. The 27-year-old has been without a club since leaving German Bundesliga side Augsburg in May 2025 but has been training with the Ravens this season. He last played a competitive professional match in November 2022 before suffering a number of injuries which led to his eventual release by Augsburg. Oxford started his career in Tottenham Hotspur's academy but joined West Ham in 2014, where he operated both in defensive midfield and at the back. He made eight Premier League appearances for the Hammers, including a player of the match display on his debut in a 2-0 win at Arsenal in August 2015, aged 16. Following loan spells with Reading and Borussia Monchengladbach, Oxford joined Augsburg in 2018 and played 77 times in the German top flight, scoring two goals. Oxford is the first signing Bromley have made under new manager Karl Robinson, who replaced Andy Woodman as boss earlier this month . "The new gaffer came in, hopefully I can help him out now, help the team and we can get some wins," Oxford told the club website , external . "I've been here for a few weeks now getting my fitness levels up. Everyone has been great. All I can do is give something back to them now." pages.text: Reference Files Reference Files Skip Navigation Within Census Geographies Reference Files Geographic Reference Files are documents that list codes for geographic entities. These include Relationship Files, Gazetteer Files, Block Assignment Files, and Tally Files. Relationship Files describe geographic relationships over time and between types. Geographic Relationships Over Time show the relationships (comparability) for the same type of geography over different periods of time (e.g. the relationship between places in 2010 and 2000). Geographic Relationships Between Entity Types show the relationship between different types of geography for the same period (e.g. the relationships between congressional districts and places). Gazetteer Files list geographic entities, such as county, place, and census tracts, with information on name, geographic code, population, housing unit counts, and latitude/longitude of the internal point. Block Assignment Files (BAFs) are among the geographic products that the Census Bureau provides to states and other data users containing the small area census data necessary for legislative redistricting. Tally Files provide the total number of geographic entities for a given area. Reference linking enables researchers to follow a link from the reference list to other full-text documents, helping them to make connections and discover new things.

Reference Linking means including Crossref DOIs (displayed as URLs) in the reference lists that you provide in your own published work.  This enables researchers to follow a link from a reference list to the current landing page for that referenced work. And because it’s a DOI rather than just a link, it will remain persistent.

All five launch events were well attended and had the participation of high-level government officials and a wide group of stakeholders. Regional Direct Air Capture Hubs Background Direct air capture (DAC) is a process that separates carbon dioxide (CO2) from the air, helping to reduce legacy CO2 in the atmosphere. The separated CO2 can then be safely and permanently stored deep underground or converted into useful carbon-containing products like concrete that prevent its release back into the atmosphere. Widespread deployment of innovative DAC technologies that capture emissions are key to reinforcing our nation’s global competitiveness and delivering new economic opportunities for American communities and industries. Program Overview The Regional DAC Hubs Program helps to accelerate the demonstration and deployment of DAC technologies. OCED’s DAC Hubs Program will develop four domestic direct air capture hubs. Each will demonstrate a DAC technology or suite of technologies at a commercial scale with the potential for capturing at least 1 million metric tons of CO2 annually from the atmosphere. Once captured, the CO2 will be permanently stored in a geologic formation or converted into new products. US$ 35.1 million Contributions to RBSA totalled US$ 35.1 million in 2024-25. In 2024–25, eleven governments are providing core voluntary funding to the ILO: Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Spain, and Qatar. These contributions, totalling US$ 35.1 million, are channelled through the ILO’s Regular Budget Supplementary Account (RBSA) and reflect sustained confidence in the ILO’s mandate and delivery capacity. This funding modality provides flexible, unearmarked resources, enabling the ILO to allocate funding strategically and respond effectively to evolving priorities. The RBSA is a central component of the ILO’s funding framework, supporting coherence, adaptability, and results across the Organization’s work. RBSA funding translates directly into impact at country level. It supports the development of innovative approaches, enables timely responses to emerging needs, expands the reach and scale of proven programmes, and promotes the integration of cross-cutting priorities in labour policies and interventions. In addition, RBSA resources help leverage complementary funding and strengthen partnerships with UN agencies, enhancing the effectiveness and sustainability of ILO support. pages.text: Reliving Mike Ditka’s legendary 7th-inning stretch rendition Skip to Content Mike Ditka, who passed away on Friday at 86 years old, was known for a lot of things. He was the first tight end inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Ditka also helped the Bears to their first and only Super Bowl victory as their head coach in the 1985 season. And for those lucky enough to be at Wrigley Field on July 5, 1998, they might know Ditka for his fiery, off-tune rendition of “Take Me Out To The Ball Game.” Ditka’s dramatics included a last-second entrance, his booming voice, and a pace so quick the stadium organist could barely keep up. As is tradition at Wrigley Field, a special guest helps lead the seventh-inning stretch. Everyone from Pearl Jam star Eddie Vedder to the Cookie Monster and everyone in between has attempted to fill the shoes of the legendary Harry Caray, who popularized the tradition. Caray died in February 1998, and the Cubs added a star-studded lineup of guest conductors including Vedder, Ernie Banks, Jay Leno, Jimmy Buffett and more. On that summer day in 1998, Ditka joined Cubs TV broadcasters Chip Caray and Steve Stone to sing the tune. Eventually, that is. Fans at the Friendly Confines began to boo with Ditka initially absent from the broadcast booth. Just as the organist played the first note, Ditka filed into the booth and grabbed the microphone. pages.text: Remembering Vincent Barabba Remembering Vincent Barabba Skip Navigation Within Census Blogs Remembering Vincent Barabba September 28, 2026 Written by: George M. Cook, Performing the Duties of Director I am saddened to share the news of the passing of former Census Bureau Director Vincent Barabba, who had just celebrated his 92nd birthday earlier this month. Barabba was born in 1934 in Chicago, Illinois. After earning his undergraduate degree from Woodbury Business College in 1954, he enlisted in the Air Force and served from 1954 until 1958. After his stint in the military, he attended California State University, Northridge, and eventually earned his M.B.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles in 1964. Barabba became president of Datamatics, Inc. in 1966, and was later named chairman of the board of Decision Making Information. He served as chairman until 1973, when he was tapped by President Nixon to serve as director of the Census Bureau. Barabba resigned as director in 1976, taking a job as manager of market research for the Xerox Corporation. He returned to the Census Bureau in 1979, however, to help guide the collection and tabulation of the 1980 Census before resigning again in 1981. He was the first and, to date, the only director of the Census Bureau to be appointed by two different presidents. In fact, he was the first person since the establishment of a permanent Census Bureau to ever serve two separate tours as official director. Souhaitez-vous faire intervenir Sally lors de l’une de vos conférences ? Envoyez un e-mail à [email protected] . Sally Wentworth Présidente-directrice générale de l’Internet Society et de la Fondation Internet Society, Sally dirige ces deux organisations, dont la mission est de bâtir et de promouvoir un Internet pour tout le monde. Elle travaille au sein de l’Internet Society depuis plus de 17 ans et en est devenue la PDG en 2024. Avant de rejoindre l’Internet Society, Sally a travaillé au Bureau de la politique scientifique et technologique de la Maison-Blanche (White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, OSTP) et au Département d’État des États-Unis (US Department of State). Ces expériences ont nourri une passion qui l’accompagne depuis toujours : renforcer le dialogue entre les décideurs et la communauté technique d’Internet. Sally est fermement convaincue que l’Internet est une ressource de développement social et économique et, dans son travail, elle adopte une approche prioritairement axée sur les personnes. En tant que PDG, elle interagit avec la communauté sur des enjeux cruciaux qui affectent Internet. Elle promeut l’impact international et profondément transformateur du travail accompli par l’Internet Society. Reoccurring, Emerging, and Persisting Enteric Bacterial Strains For Public Health Aug. 17, 2026 What to know Some enteric bacterial strains cause acute outbreaks linked to specific sources. Other strains, referred to as reoccurring, emerging, or persisting (REP) strains, can reoccur and periodically cause acute outbreaks. REP strains can also emerge and increase in frequency or persist and cause illnesses over periods of months or years, despite investigation and prevention efforts. Identifying REP strains Investigators use a laboratory method called whole genome sequencing (WGS) to identify the DNA fingerprints of bacteria from ill people and from foods, animals, and the environment. These DNA fingerprints represent strains of bacteria. Investigators use these DNA fingerprints to find outbreaks of enteric (gastrointestinal) diseases. When scientists identify a group of people who got sick around the same time with a strain with the same DNA fingerprint, this represents a possible outbreak. Reporting Health and Safety Data Under TSCA section 8(d) Under TSCA section 8(d), EPA has the authority to promulgate rules to require producers, importers, and (if specified) processors of a chemical substance or mixture to submit lists and/or copies of unpublished (both ongoing and completed) health and safety studies. Chemicals designated or recommended for testing by the TSCA Interagency Testing Committee (ITC) may be added to the rule via immediate final rulemaking (up to 50 substances/year). Non-ITC chemicals can be added to the TSCA section 8(d) rule via notice and comment rulemaking. The term "health and safety study" is intended to be interpreted broadly and means "any study of any effect of a chemical substance or mixture on health or the environment or on both," including but not limited to: Epidemiological or clinical studies; Studies of occupational exposure; In vivo and in vitro toxicological studies; and Ecotoxicological studies. The images, although fake, can be used to blackmail children to demand money or more images. Reports of Selected Salmonella Outbreak Investigations About these resources When two or more people get the same illness from the same contaminated food, drink or animal, the event is called an enteric (intestinal) disease outbreak. The list on this page primarily represents multistate outbreak investigations involving Salmonella in the last two years where CDC was the lead public health agency. For a complete listing of reported outbreaks please use the National Outbreak Reporting System (NORS) Dashboard . Public health officials investigate outbreaks to control them, so more people do not get sick, and to learn how to prevent similar outbreaks from happening in the future.
